key_insight: In generally healthy adults, some modifiable dementia risk factors were associated with cognitive performance, while emerging Alzheimer’s pathology was associated with faster cognitive decline.
clinical_relevance: The findings distinguish cognitive performance from subsequent decline but do not establish that changing risk factors prevents decline.
method: Analyzed 1,396 adults aged 36–108 across 2,878 visits, with mean follow-up of 5.0 years.
Tested 18 risk factors against three cognitive outcomes, separating performance from subsequent decline.
Examined plasma neurodegenerative disease biomarkers and repeated risk-factor analyses in pTau217-negative participants.
evidence_signal: Education, diabetes, low motor function, hearing loss and low vision were associated with performance (FDR q < 0.05), but none with decline; pTau217 positivity was associated with faster PACC decline (−0.058 SD/year, p < 0.001).
watch_item: These observational findings in generally healthy adults do not establish causality and may not generalize to clinical dementia populations.
paper_title: Cognition in healthy aging, ages 36 to 108: Associations with dementia risk factors and neurodegenerative disease biomarkers
